question: Does the review loop, rather than the reviewer prompt or the model family, account for the cross-family gap measured at 3429f759ceef?

inherits.grader_change: One change, before any model call of this lane: `loadRuns` now reads run files in run-id order. The cluster bootstrap resamples cluster indices from a seeded PRNG, so the order clusters were built in - a readdir order - decided the published interval. The detection rule, the window, the patterns, the pass rule and the exclusion of errored runs are untouched. Re-grading the first eval's committed runs moves exactly one published number: the crossfamily cluster bootstrap lower bound, 21.7% to 21.1%. Every rate, count and other bound is identical.
inherits.note: The 30 findings, the 3 heads, the detection rule (`detects`, window_chars 1200) and the interval code are taken unchanged from the first eval so the two can be compared. `rounds.ts` only composes per-run detections into sequences; it never redefines detection. `rounds.test.ts` proves it, by reproducing from the first eval's committed runs its published per-arm rates and bootstraps, its candidate-minus-control of -3.3 pp, its crossfamily-minus-control of +11.7 pp, and its symlink-class Fisher p of 0.0099.

unit_of_analysis.sequence: (head, trial) under one arm; a one-round arm's sequence is its single run
unit_of_analysis.primary_score: union over rounds: a finding counts for a sequence when the frozen rule fires on at least one round's report in that sequence
secondary_scores: final-round-only: the frozen rule on the last round's report alone
per-round marginal: findings first detected at round 1, at round 2, at round 3
unit_of_analysis.rationale: The corpus being graded against was harvested across all rounds of each night-time review, so the union is the quantity that corpus measures. Grading each round separately and OR-ing avoids window artefacts at a concatenation seam.

held_fixed.appended_system_prompt: prompts/candidate.md in every arm, same family and cross family
held_fixed.round_1_user_prompt: generated by the same `userPrompt` function in run.ts that the one-round arms used, with the same head, the same 20 minutes and a per-run scratch path, so round 1 of every multi-round sequence is a fresh replication of the one-round arm and serves as the provider-drift check. The only text that differs is the scratch path, which is per run in both.

budget_change_declared.what: A three-round arm gets three 20-minute budgets, so its total wall-clock and token budget is 3x the one-round arm's.
budget_change_declared.why_not_silent: That is the treatment, not a harness tweak. The `retry-blind` arm holds attempts and total budget equal to `rounds-carry` while carrying nothing, so the attempts/budget component is measured separately from the carried-information component.
budget_change_declared.why_not_a_longer_single_round: The first eval measured every arm stopping at 4-6 minutes of a 20-minute budget with none cut off; more wall clock inside one session is not a treatment the model takes up. A fresh context is what forces another attempt.

arms.name: retry-blind
arms.carries: only the fact that an earlier attempt was incomplete; fresh context and a fresh scratch directory each round

arms.name: rounds-carry
arms.carries: every earlier round's report verbatim, an instruction not to re-report what they found, and the sequence's scratch directory with their probes, fixtures and output still in it

round_prompt_templates.note: Appended to the round-1 user prompt for rounds 2 and above. {N} is the round, {TOTAL} the arm's round count, {PRIOR} = {N}-1. Both templates state the same expectation - an earlier attempt missed something - so the only difference between the arms is whether that attempt's content is present.
round_prompt_templates.retry-blind: This is attempt {N} of {TOTAL} at reviewing this same change. {PRIOR} earlier attempt(s) have already reviewed it and missed defects that a later reviewer found. You are not being shown what they reported, what they ran, or where they looked. Start from the change itself and find what they missed.

comparisons.name: loop
comparisons.reads: does the review loop close any of the gap a better prompt did not

comparisons.name: carried-information
comparisons.reads: does what a round carries matter beyond getting another attempt

comparisons.name: another-attempt
comparisons.reads: does a second and third cold attempt alone add findings

comparisons.name: family-vs-loop
comparisons.reads: does one cross-family round still beat three same-family rounds

comparisons.name: drift
comparisons.test: round 1 of retry-blind and rounds-carry (12 fresh runs) - single (6 reused runs)
comparisons.reads: whether the reused one-round arms are still a valid baseline

intervals.per_arm: Wilson over (finding, sequence) pairs and a cluster bootstrap over sequences, both from grade.ts, 10000 iterations, seed 20261030
intervals.paired: cluster bootstrap over the six (head, trial) pairs, resampling pairs with replacement, 10000 iterations, seed 20261030
intervals.report_rule: n and the 95% interval always; never a bare delta

symlink_class.defined_from: the first eval's post-hoc subgroup, reproduced from its committed runs: same-family 0 of 18 (finding, run) pairs, cross-family 3 of 6, Fisher two-sided p = 0.0099
symlink_class.question: with rounds in play, does this class stay family-bound, or does a later round reach it
symlink_class.test: Fisher exact, two-sided, over (finding, sequence) pairs in this class, rounds-carry against crossfamily-single and against single

cost.basis: the first eval's measured $1.58 per same-family run for 18 retry-blind runs and 6 rounds-carry round-1 runs, and $2.50 for each of the 12 rounds-carry later rounds, which carry 6-15 KB more input
cost.enforcement: run-rounds.ts tracks cumulative spend and refuses to start another sequence once the cap is reached; a run stopped by the per-round --max-cost exits 3 and is recorded as an error, never as a score

dropped_arms.arm: fix-carried: round N reviews the head that fixed round N-1's findings
dropped_arms.why: Only pr17394-r7 -> pr17394-r8 is a consecutive-head pair among the three heads with working trees, and only 1 of #17394's 23 corpus findings was closed by a later head, so r8 is new feature code rather than a fix of r7. The arm would confound attacking a fix with reviewing new code at n = 1 head.
The per-round marginal inside the three-round arms gives the dose-response at round 1, 2 and 3 for no extra model calls.

At the first eval's $5.09 per cross-family run it costs about $92 on its own, more than this whole run, and the question asked is whether the loop explains the same-family gap, not whether rounds also help cross family.
Covered under budget_change_declared: every arm of the first eval self-terminated at 4-6 minutes of 20.

dropped_arms.arm: decomposing the carry bundle into findings-only, scratch-only and closure-only
dropped_arms.why: Three more arms at n = 60 each could not resolve a three-way decomposition of an effect whose existence is not yet established. The first question is whether the bundle moves anything at all.
